h is an integer with h>=0

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix integers m>=2 and h>=0. Define f:K_{m,h}→Z^(m-1) by f(x)=w where for each i∈{1,...,m-1}, w_i = m x_i + i. Let A_{m,h} be the set of tuples w=(w_1,...,w_{m-1})∈Z^(m-1) satisfying: (1) ∀i, w_i >= m+i and w_i ≡ i (mod m); (2) Σ_{i=1}^{m-1} w_i = m h + m(m-1)/2; (3) ∀i,j∈{1,...,m-1}, if i+j<m then w_i+w_j >= w_{i+j}, and if i+j>m then w_i+w_j >= w_{i+j-m} (no constraint asserted for i+j=m). Then f is a bijection from K_{m,h} onto A_{m,h}, with inverse g:A_{m,h}→K_{m,h} given coordinatewise by g(w)_i = (w_i - i)/m. Equivalently: (i) ∀x∈K_{m,h}, f(x)∈A_{m,h}; (ii) ∀w∈A_{m,h}, g(w)∈K_{m,h} and f(g(w))=w; (iii) g(f(x))=x for all x∈K_{m,h}.
quantifier_order: For all integers m, if m>=2

For all tuples x in K_{m,h}
For all indices i,j in {1,...,m-1}, conditions are applied casewise by whether i+j<m, i+j=m, or i+j>m
For all tuples w in A_{m,h}
There exists a tuple x (uniquely determined) with x_i=(w_i-i)/m such that x in K_{m,h} and f(x)=w

shared_context.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously with coordinate sum g+1. Then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let h be an integer with h >= 0. Define K_{m,h} to be the set of all tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=h and such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i+j < m then x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i+j > m then x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m}. For x in K_{m,h}, define w=(w_1,...,w_{m-1}) by w_i = m x_i + i for each i. Then x -> w is a bijection from K_{m,h} onto the set A_{m,h} of all tuples w=(w_1,...,w_{m-1}) of integers satisfying the following conditions: for every i in {1,...,m-1}, one has w_i >= m+i and w_i is congruent to i modulo m; one has w_1+...+w_{m-1} = m h + m(m-1)/2; and for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i+j < m then w_i+w_j >= w_{i+j}, and if i+j > m then w_i+w_j >= w_{i+j-m}. The inverse map is x_i = (w_i - i)/m.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix integers m>=2 and h>=0. Define f:K_{m,h}\to \mathbb Z^{m-1} by
f(x_1,\dots,x_{m-1})=(w_1,\dots,w_{m-1}),\qquad w_i:=mx_i+i\quad (1\le i\le m-1).
We prove that f is a bijection from K_{m,h} onto A_{m,h}, and that the inverse is given by
g(w)_i=\frac{w_i-i}{m}.

We proceed in three parts.

1. For every x\in K_{m,h}, one has f(x)\in A_{m,h}.

Let x=(x_1,\dots,x_{m-1})\in K_{m,h}, and put w=f(x).
We verify the defining conditions of A_{m,h}.

(a) Lower bounds and congruences.
Since each x_i is a positive integer, x_i\ge 1. Hence
w_i=mx_i+i\ge m+i.
Also w_i-i=mx_i is divisible by m, so w_i\equiv i\pmod m.
Thus the first condition in the definition of A_{m,h} holds.

(b) Sum condition.
Because x_1+\cdots+x_{m-1}=h,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{m-1} w_i
=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}(mx_i+i)
=m\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}x_i+\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}i
=mh+\frac{m(m-1)}2.
\]
So the second condition holds.

(c) Inequalities.
Take any i,j\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}.

If i+j<m, then since x\in K_{m,h},
\[
x_i+x_j\ge x_{i+j}.
\]
Multiplying by m and adding i+j gives
\[
mx_i+i+mx_j+j\ge mx_{i+j}+i+j.
\]
Since i+j<m, the right-hand side is exactly w_{i+j}. Therefore
\[
w_i+w_j\ge w_{i+j}.
\]

If i+j>m, then since x\in K_{m,h},
\[
x_i+x_j+1\ge x_{i+j-m}.
\]
Multiplying by m gives
\[
mx_i+mx_j+m\ge mx_{i+j-m}.
\]
Adding i+j-m to both sides yields
\[
mx_i+mx_j+i+j\ge mx_{i+j-m}+(i+j-m).
\]
But the left-hand side is w_i+w_j, and the right-hand side is w_{i+j-m}. Hence
\[
w_i+w_j\ge w_{i+j-m}.
\]
Thus the third condition also holds.

Therefore w\in A_{m,h}. This proves f(K_{m,h})\subseteq A_{m,h}.

2. For every w\in A_{m,h}, the tuple g(w) belongs to K_{m,h}, and f(g(w))=w.

Let w=(w_1,\dots,w_{m-1})\in A_{m,h}. Define x=(x_1,\dots,x_{m-1}) by
\[
x_i:=\frac{w_i-i}{m}\qquad(1\le i\le m-1).
\]
We must show x\in K_{m,h}.

(a) Each x_i is a positive integer.
Because w_i\equiv i\pmod m, the difference w_i-i is divisible by m, so x_i\in\mathbb Z.
Because w_i\ge m+i,
\[
x_i=\frac{w_i-i}{m}\ge \frac{m+i-i}{m}=1.
\]
So each x_i is a positive integer.

(b) Sum condition.
Using the defining sum condition for A_{m,h},
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}x_i
=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}\frac{w_i-i}{m}
=\frac{1}{m}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}w_i-\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}i\right)
=\frac{1}{m}\left(mh+\frac{m(m-1)}2-\frac{m(m-1)}2\right)=h.
\]
Thus x_1+\cdots+x_{m-1}=h.

(c) Inequalities.
Take any i,j\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}.

If i+j<m, then since w\in A_{m,h},
\[
w_i+w_j\ge w_{i+j}.
\]
Substituting w_k=mx_k+k for k=i,j,i+j gives
\[
(mx_i+i)+(mx_j+j)\ge mx_{i+j}+(i+j).
\]
Cancel i+j and divide by m to obtain
\[
x_i+x_j\ge x_{i+j}.
\]

If i+j>m, then since w\in A_{m,h},
\[
w_i+w_j\ge w_{i+j-m}.
\]
Substituting w_k=mx_k+k gives
\[
(mx_i+i)+(mx_j+j)\ge mx_{i+j-m}+(i+j-m).
\]
Rearranging,
\[
m(x_i+x_j)+m\ge mx_{i+j-m},
\]
so dividing by m yields
\[
x_i+x_j+1\ge x_{i+j-m}.
\]
Thus the defining inequalities for K_{m,h} hold.

Therefore x\in K_{m,h}.

Now compute, for each i,
\[
f(g(w))_i = m\left(\frac{w_i-i}{m}\right)+i = w_i.
\]
Hence f(g(w))=w.

So every w\in A_{m,h} has a preimage under f, namely g(w), and that preimage lies in K_{m,h}. This proves A_{m,h}\subseteq f(K_{m,h}). Combined with Part 1, we get f(K_{m,h})=A_{m,h}.

3. The maps f and g are inverse to each other on their domains.

We already proved in Part 2 that for every w\in A_{m,h},
\[
f(g(w))=w.
\]
Now let x\in K_{m,h}. If w=f(x), then w_i=mx_i+i, so
\[
g(f(x))_i=\frac{w_i-i}{m}=\frac{mx_i+i-i}{m}=x_i.
\]
Thus g(f(x))=x.

Therefore g is a two-sided inverse of f, so f is a bijection from K_{m,h} onto A_{m,h}. The inverse is exactly the coordinatewise formula
\[
g(w)_i=\frac{w_i-i}{m}.
\]
This is precisely the claimed statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Defined f(x)_i=mx_i+i. Verified directly that any x in K_{m,h} maps to a tuple satisfying the lower bounds, congruences, sum condition, and homogenized inequalities of A_{m,h}. Conversely, for w in A_{m,h}, the formula x_i=(w_i-i)/m gives positive integers, preserves the total sum h, and converts the inequalities of A_{m,h} back to those of K_{m,h}. Finally, checked f(g(w))=w and g(f(x))=x coordinatewise, so f is a bijection with inverse g.

used_external_facts: Sum of the first m-1 integers: 1+2+...+(m-1)=m(m-1)/2.
